status_summary: Secretary Rubio announced a reorganization on 2025-04-22 that, per AP, would cut domestic staff by 15 percent and consolidate 734 bureaus and offices into 602 (State's own statement is general and does not mention political leadership of bureaus), and on 2025-07-11 State sent reduction-in-force notices to about 1,100 civil servants and nearly 250 Foreign Service officers, saying changes would be complete by 2025-08-04, that nearly 3,000 members of the workforce would depart in all and that no further reductions in force were planned (per Nextgov). Civil-service employees were separated on 2025-09-11 according to a complaint filed by affected employees on 2026-02-13 (an allegation, not a finding), while the Foreign Service separations were delayed by Section 120 of Public Law 119-37, which barred reduction-in-force actions through 2026-01-30, and by a 2025-12-17 preliminary injunction from a federal court in San Francisco through the same date; on 2026-01-09 the judge said the order did not reach the July notices, the government withdrew its appeal, and State declined to rescind the July notices. A statement from the office of Senator Andy Kim dated 2026-05-06 says State had officially terminated over 200 Foreign Service officers, and a House release of 2026-05-22 refers to more than 200 members separated in May; State's FY2027 budget justification projects about 11,000 Foreign Service and 6,000 civil service employees, down from over 14,000 and nearly 13,000 before 2025 (as reported by Federal News Network). In 2026-06-03 testimony, State's Office of Inspector General called the reorganization and integration of selected USAID functions the department's main staffing and organizational challenge.

timeline.event: Rubio announced a department-wide reorganization: 15% cut in US-based staff, more than 100 bureaus closed or consolidated (734 bureaus and offices reduced to 602), and a new office for foreign and humanitarian affairs; State's spokesperson called it a roadmap rather than immediate firings.

State publishes a statement titled Building an America First State Department announcing a comprehensive reorganization plan in general terms: consolidating region-specific functions, removing redundant offices and ending programs not required by statute that it views as out of line with core national interests. The page names no bureaus, staffing numbers or leadership changes (it is undated; date from contemporaneous reporting).

The Supreme Court stayed a district-court injunction against Executive Order 14210 (agency workforce reductions and reorganization plans) while appeals proceed, saying the government was likely to succeed on its argument that the order is lawful and expressing no view on any specific agency plan.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: State issued reduction-in-force notices to more than 1,300 employees: over 1,100 civil servants (60 days' notice) and nearly 250 Foreign Service staff serving domestically (120 days' notice).

State civil-service employees who received reduction-in-force notices on 2025-07-11 were separated on this date, according to a complaint filed by former federal employees in the District of Maryland on 2026-02-13 (allegations in a court filing, not findings); the same complaint alleges that one Foreign Service officer was separated through an involuntary resignation on 2025-11-16.
timeline.source: Complaint, No. 8:26-cv-00573 (D. Md.), copy hosted by dclawcollective.com

timeline.event: The stopgap funding law that ended the 43-day shutdown, Public Law 119-37, takes effect. Its Section 120 bars federal funds for initiating, noticing or carrying out a reduction in force through 2026-01-30 and gives no force or effect to RIFs taken between 2025-10-01 and enactment, with exceptions for voluntary separations, court-ordered actions and orderly shutdown actions; State and unions disagreed on whether it covered the notices issued in July (per Federal News Network).
State sent an updated notice setting Foreign Service separations for 2025-12-05; later in December a federal judge in San Francisco (Judge Illston) enjoined State and other agencies' layoffs.

Per a case tracker summary, the court in AFGE v. OMB (N.D. Cal. No. 3:25-cv-08302, Judge Illston) granted a temporary restraining order against a State Department reduction in force scheduled for 2025-12-05; the order itself was not read.

Judge Illston (N.D. Cal.), in a suit led by federal employee unions including AFSA, issues a preliminary injunction directing State, Education, the SBA and GSA to rescind reduction-in-force notices for employees terminated during the shutdown and barring further steps to carry out a reduction in force through 2026-01-30; nearly 250 State Foreign Service officers were affected, per news reports.

At a 2026-01-09 hearing Judge Illston said her order covered only State's updated 2025-12-02 notice and did not require rescinding the July notices, without issuing a new formal order; the government had appealed the December order and then withdrawn the appeal, and State said it would not send rescission notices for about 250 Foreign Service officers.

Federal News Network reported (month-level date) that State's FY2027 budget justification projects about 11,000 Foreign Service and 6,000 civil service employees, that the officers with RIF notices had been on paid leave for nine months, and that a senior official told House members there were no plans to reinstate them.

A statement from the office of Senator Andy Kim says State has officially terminated over 200 Foreign Service officers while still recruiting new officers; it gives no effective date and does not describe the terminations as a reduction in force. A House release of 2026-05-22 from Rep. Johnny Olszewski and colleagues refers to more than 200 Foreign Service members separated in May 2026.

State's Office of Inspector General testifies to a Senate appropriations subcommittee that the reorganization and the integration of selected USAID functions, on a compressed timeline, were the main staffing challenge, and recommends an implementation plan with milestones; the testimony does not discuss staff cuts or bureau consolidation.
timeline.source: State Department Office of Inspector General

title: Reorganize State to cut offices and overhead and tighten political control
uncertainties: State's reorganization statement on its own site (state.gov) could not be fetched (client error, last on 2026-10-22), and on 2026-10-26 neither its URL nor that of State's 2025-05-29 statement appeared in search results; an archive copy could not be opened. The 2025-05-29 statement (Next Steps on Building an America First State Department) was read on 2026-10-26 in a copy hosted by GlobalSecurity.org: it says State notified Congress that day of how it planned to carry out the reorganization and gives no figures, which matches the 2025-05-29 date of the notification letter known through the external retrieval. The 2025-04-22 statement is general and gives no numbers by the account of the earlier review, so the figures come from AP and Federal News Network and describe the plan, not a verified end state. An external retrieval reported figures from the congressional notification letter of 2025-05-29 (more than 300 of 734 bureaus and offices streamlined, merged or eliminated, 3,448 domestic positions cut from 18,780, an 18 percent staff reduction) and a Foreign Service separation date of 2025-11-10; the letter figures are known only through that retrieval, the letter itself is not public in full according to the retrieval, and they are not stated as verified. They differ in form from the AP figures in the record (15 percent cut, 734 offices reduced to 602) and the difference was not reconciled. Read in an earlier check: Nextgov (2025-07-11) confirms notices to about 1,100 civil servants and nearly 250 Foreign Service officers on 2025-07-11, 60 and 120 day notice periods, a completion date of 2025-08-04 and no plans for further reductions in force; a complaint filed on 2026-02-13 in the District of Maryland (No. 8:26-cv-00573, read on a copy hosted by a plaintiffs' counsel collective; the court docket was not reached) alleges that State plaintiffs received notices on 2025-07-11 and civil service plaintiffs were separated on 2025-09-11, with one Foreign Service officer separated by involuntary resignation on 2025-11-16 (plaintiffs' allegations). On 2026-10-26 three filings in AFGE v. OMB (N.D. Cal. No. 3:25-cv-08302-SI) were read as RECAP copies on CourtListener: the revised second amended complaint of 2025-10-28 (ECF 92) quotes an OMB lapse memorandum directing agencies to consider RIF notices; the supplemental complaint of 2025-12-03 (ECF 121-1) alleges that State issued RIF notices to approximately 1,300 Foreign Service and civil service employees on 2025-07-11 with a 2025-11-10 separation date for about 250 Foreign Service employees, so the 2025-11-10 date now also appears as a plaintiffs' allegation in a court filing; and a plaintiffs' counsel declaration of 2026-01-06 (ECF 147-1) records State's position that the preliminary injunction did not require rescinding the July notices. These are party filings, not findings, and the about 1,300 total differs slightly from the Nextgov count of about 1,100 plus nearly 250. The FY2027 budget justification and State's organizational chart were not opened. The temporary restraining order date, case number and appeal number rest on a case tracker (Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse) whose docket summary has no 2026 entries, and the court orders themselves were not opened. The injunction's 2026-01-30 end date and the appeal withdrawal are confirmed by news reports. A settlement agreement in the RIF cases dated September 2026 appeared in search results only as a Courthouse News upload and was not opened; its terms and any effect on State's separations are unknown. The May 2026 separations rest on releases from the office of Senator Andy Kim (2026-05-06) and of Rep. Johnny Olszewski (2026-05-22), not on a State record; a House letter reports about 250 separations in the week of 2026-05-11 as a reported, unconfirmed figure, so the count and date differ across sources. A statement by AFSA, a professional association and interested party, places the separations in the week of 2026-05-05; it is an unverified lead at low confidence, not confirmed by an official document or news report found. No source in this record shows a change to political control of bureaus, which the Mandate's recommendation mentions. A limited search found no court ruling on the May 2026 separations, no fiscal 2027 reduction-in-force bar and no State authorization bill. A State weekly bulletin sent on 2025-04-25 from State's GovDelivery account was opened: its section on the reorganization says the Secretary announced the plan on 2025-04-23 and gives no numbers, bureau counts or percentages. The record keeps 2025-04-22 for the announcement (AP and the earlier retrieval); the one-day conflict with the bulletin's 2025-04-23 was not resolved, and the bulletin is a weekly summary, not the statement.
